courseTitle: How IT Teams Work: Agile, Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban & Software Releases

slots.practicalActivity: Watch both lessons, then write a one-paragraph comparison of Agile vs. Waterfall in your own words, and draft 3 sample user stories ("As a ___, I want ___, so that ___") for a fictional 'add a login page' feature, sized to fit in one 2-week sprint.
slots.deliverable: A written Agile-vs-Waterfall comparison paragraph, plus 3 sprint-ready user stories.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a simple Kanban board (a free tool like Trello, or even a 4-column table on paper) with To Do / In Progress / Review / Done, and place the 3 user stories from the previous hour on it. Then write, for each story, which SDLC environment (Dev, QA, UAT, Production) it would move through before it's considered live.
slots.deliverable: A populated Kanban board with the 3 user stories, plus a written Dev → QA → UAT → Production path for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a free GitHub account if you don't already have one. Initialize a practice repository, make at least 3 commits with clear, descriptive commit messages, and open one pull request against a second branch. Then write a short explanation of 2-3 checks a CI/CD pipeline would typically run automatically before that pull request is allowed to merge.
slots.deliverable: A GitHub repository link with 3+ real commits and 1 pull request, plus a written explanation of what a CI/CD pipeline checks before merging.

slots.practicalActivity: Complete the Real-World IT Project Simulation lesson's exercise end to end. Then write a half-page reflection connecting Agile/Scrum, Kanban, Git, and CI/CD to what you just simulated — specifically, where in the simulation each concept actually showed up.
slots.deliverable: The completed simulation exercise, plus a written reflection tying Agile, Kanban, Git, and CI/CD together.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: Can explain Agile vs. Waterfall and Scrum/Kanban in plain language, has made real commits and opened a pull request on GitHub, and can describe what a CI/CD pipeline checks before a release ships.
